PROJECT OBJECTIVE

I want to upgrade the visual design of my existing IMPOSTER party game.

The chosen direction is:

PREMIUM EDITORIAL — Warm Ivory, Forest Green, Electric Lime, Soft Gradients and Subtle Paper Texture.

The goal is to make the application look significantly more polished, attractive, modern and professionally designed.

I want the game to feel like a carefully designed premium party-game product, rather than a basic web application.

IMPORTANT:

This is a VISUAL DESIGN UPDATE ONLY.

Preserve the complete existing game functionality, game logic, data, settings, interactions and mechanics.

Do not rebuild the application.

Do not remove or simplify existing features.

---

1. DESIGN DIRECTION

Create a consistent visual identity based on these characteristics:

- Premium editorial design.
- Warm and sophisticated colour palette.
- Soft natural gradients.
- Subtle paper-like texture.
- Elegant typography.
- Beautifully layered cards.
- Refined buttons and controls.
- Clean spacing and visual hierarchy.
- Modern, smooth and restrained interactions.

The design should feel premium but remain playful enough for a party game.

Avoid making it look like a corporate dashboard.

Avoid making it look like a generic template.

---

2. COLOUR SYSTEM

Use the following palette as the foundation.

Main colours

Element| Colour
Main background| #EDE9DC
Secondary background| #F4F0E6
Card background| #FAF8F1
Primary dark green| #243329
Secondary green| #405B42
Main lime accent| #B9EB58
Secondary lime| #D5F2A0
Muted olive| #8AAE43
Main text| #243329
Secondary text| #77796D
Borders| #E5E0D4

Colour usage

- Use warm ivory as the primary background.
- Use forest green for important controls, headings and strong visual elements.
- Use lime green for primary actions, selected states and important highlights.
- Use muted olive for secondary information.
- Use warm white for cards and content surfaces.
- Use subtle neutral borders rather than strong outlines.

Do not introduce unrelated bright colours.

Existing semantic colours for success, warnings, errors and important game results may remain where necessary, but they should harmonise with the overall theme.

---

3. BACKGROUND — MAKE THIS A MAJOR VISUAL IMPROVEMENT

The current background feels too plain.

I want a more attractive background using a combination of gradients and subtle paper texture.

Requirements

Create a sophisticated background with:

1. A warm ivory base.
2. Very subtle cream and beige gradient transitions.
3. Extremely subtle paper-grain texture.
4. A few soft, oversized abstract gradient shapes.
5. Very restrained lime and olive colour accents.
6. Natural visual depth without clutter.

The background should feel elegant, warm and premium.

Important implementation details

- Texture must remain extremely subtle.
- Gradients must not interfere with text readability.
- Decorative shapes should sit behind the interface.
- Do not make the background visually noisy.
- Do not use large photographs.
- Do not use distracting repeating patterns.
- Avoid excessive blur or heavy visual effects.

If a texture asset is needed, create or use a lightweight local asset.

The game must continue working offline.

Do not introduce external image dependencies or remote background requests.

Use CSS gradients and lightweight local styling wherever practical.

---

4. CARDS AND CONTENT CONTAINERS

Improve the appearance of existing cards throughout the application.

Desired appearance

- Warm white or ivory surfaces.
- Soft, natural shadows.
- Fine neutral borders.
- Consistent rounded corners.
- Better separation between different content sections.
- Clean internal spacing.
- Clear visual hierarchy.

Cards should appear slightly elevated from the background without looking excessively raised.

Maintain consistent card styling throughout all screens.

Do not change the information contained in existing cards.

Do not remove existing sections.

---

5. TYPOGRAPHY

Improve typographic consistency.

Headings

- Strong, modern and clean.
- Dark forest-green colour.
- Clear hierarchy between page titles and section headings.
- Consistent font weights.

Body text

- Comfortable to read.
- Good line spacing.
- Clear distinction between primary and secondary information.

Small labels

- Use restrained uppercase typography where appropriate.
- Preserve the editorial feel of the existing IMPOSTER branding.
- Avoid excessive letter spacing.

Do not unnecessarily replace the existing font assets or introduce external font dependencies.

Ensure text remains readable on smaller mobile screens.

---

6. BUTTONS AND INTERACTIVE ELEMENTS

Polish the appearance of all existing buttons and controls.

Primary buttons

- Bright lime background: #B9EB58.
- Dark forest-green text.
- Rounded corners.
- Strong but elegant typography.
- Subtle interaction feedback.

Secondary buttons

- Dark forest-green background where appropriate.
- Warm white text.
- Consistent rounded corners.

Outlined buttons

- Warm white or transparent surfaces.
- Fine neutral borders.
- Dark green text.

Toggle switches

Improve the appearance of existing toggles while preserving their functionality.

Use:

- Lime or muted green for ON.
- Soft neutral grey for OFF.
- Clear thumb positioning.
- Smooth but restrained transitions.

Interactive states

Ensure existing controls have consistent:

- Default states.
- Pressed states.
- Selected states.
- Disabled states.
- Focus states.

Buttons should feel responsive and polished.

Do not change their underlying actions.

Do not rename existing controls or change their intended behaviour.

---

7. APPLY THE DESIGN CONSISTENTLY ACROSS THE ENTIRE GAME

This is extremely important.

Do not apply the new design only to the home screen.

Every existing screen must use the same visual identity.

Inspect the complete application and update the styling of all existing screens, including:

A. Home screen

- IMPOSTER branding.
- Main heading.
- Party selector.
- New Party control.
- Party statistics.
- Player management.
- Player cards.
- Randomize order.
- Setup sections.

B. Game setup

- Number of Imposters.
- Final word guess.
- Imposter hint toggle.
- Typed clue toggle.
- Discussion timer.
- Word category selection.
- Start Game button.

C. Private role reveal

- Player reveal screen.
- Reveal My Role button.
- Normal player role presentation.
- Imposter role presentation.
- Secret-word presentation.
- Category presentation.
- Hint presentation.
- Pass-the-phone instructions.

Keep the privacy and reveal behaviour unchanged.

D. Clue and discussion screens

- Typed clue entry.
- Verbal discussion instructions.
- Random starting player presentation.
- Discussion timer.
- Continue controls.

E. Voting area

- Player voting cards.
- Vote selection.
- Skip Vote.
- Voting progress.
- Vote submission.
- Voting results.
- Elimination presentation.

Preserve the existing voting theme and functionality, but bring its visual styling into the new design system.

F. Final guess phase

- Existing final word guessing interface.
- Guess submission.
- Success and failure presentations.

G. Match results

- Winner presentation.
- Secret-word reveal.
- Imposter identities.
- Voting totals.
- Final scoreboard.
- Player scores.

H. Party statistics and history

- Match history.
- Party scoreboard.
- Player statistics.
- Leaderboards.
- Empty states.

Every screen should look like it belongs to the same application.

Do not leave older screens with inconsistent colours or outdated styling.

---

8. BRANDING

Preserve the existing IMPOSTER identity.

Keep the existing logo and its general visual direction.

Improve its presentation through:

- Better spacing.
- Consistent placement.
- Appropriate contrast.
- Refined typography.
- Consistent brand colours.

Do not replace the logo unnecessarily.

Do not introduce a completely different brand identity.

---

9. MOBILE-FIRST DESIGN

This is a pass-the-phone party game, so mobile usability is extremely important.

Ensure:

- All screens work properly on narrow mobile displays.
- Cards do not overflow.
- Buttons remain easy to tap.
- Text does not become too small.
- Player grids adapt to screen width.
- Long names and labels are handled gracefully.
- Scrolling remains natural.
- The layout works on both portrait and landscape where supported.

Avoid desktop-oriented layouts that look cramped on phones.

Maintain accessible contrast.

---

10. ANIMATIONS AND TRANSITIONS

Add subtle polish to existing interactions where appropriate.

Examples:

- Gentle button press feedback.
- Smooth toggle transitions.
- Subtle card entrance transitions.
- Refined screen transitions.
- Gentle selected-state transitions.

Keep animations short and restrained.

Avoid:

- Excessive bouncing.
- Flashing effects.
- Distracting movement.
- Unnecessary animations on every element.

Respect reduced-motion preferences where supported.

Do not modify game timing, timers or gameplay sequencing to create visual effects.

---

11. PERFORMANCE AND OFFLINE REQUIREMENTS

The game must remain lightweight.

- Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
- Avoid large background images.
- Avoid excessive CSS effects that affect mobile performance.
- Keep assets local.
- Do not require an internet connection to render the theme.
- Preserve existing offline functionality.
- Avoid introducing unnecessary JavaScript for purely visual changes.

Prefer reusable styling variables, shared components and existing design infrastructure.

---

12. ABSOLUTE FUNCTIONALITY PRESERVATION

THIS IS A VISUAL UPDATE ONLY.

The following systems must remain exactly as they currently work.

Party system

- Multiple parties.
- Party switching.
- New party creation.
- Party-specific player records.
- Party history and statistics.

Player management

- 3–12 player support.
- Player creation.
- Player editing.
- Player removal.
- Duplicate-name validation.
- Player limits.
- Randomized order.

Game setup

- Imposter count.
- Category selection.
- Final word guess setting.
- Imposter hint setting.
- Typed clue setting.
- Discussion timer.

Gameplay

- Secret-word selection.
- Word reuse prevention.
- Random role assignment.
- Mandatory private role reveal.
- Imposter hints.
- Typed clues.
- Verbal discussion.
- Random starting player.
- Repeated discussion and voting rounds.
- Multiple-Imposter support.
- Private voting.
- Skip Vote.
- Tie handling.
- Player elimination.
- Victory conditions.
- Final word guess.

Results and records

- Match results.
- Scoring.
- Party scoreboard.
- Match history.
- Player statistics.
- Leaderboards.
- Local data persistence.

Do not change the logic, calculations, state transitions, data structures or storage formats of these systems.

Do not remove existing features.

Do not replace working components just for visual convenience.

---

13. DEVELOPMENT APPROACH

Before editing:

1. Inspect the entire project structure.
2. Identify the existing global styling and design system.
3. Identify shared components.
4. Identify screens with inconsistent styling.
5. Determine how the current theme is applied.
6. Plan a reusable visual update.

During implementation:

- Prefer shared theme variables.
- Reuse existing components.
- Apply consistent styling across all screens.
- Avoid unnecessary component rewrites.
- Preserve existing event handlers.
- Preserve existing state management.
- Preserve existing data flow.
- Keep changes focused on presentation.

If an existing component mixes visual styling and gameplay logic, modify only the presentation-related parts.

Do not rewrite the component's underlying functionality.

---

14. TESTING AND FINAL VERIFICATION

After the design update, verify the following:

Visual checks

- Home screen uses the new theme.
- Setup screen uses the new theme.
- Role reveal screens use the new theme.
- Discussion screens use the new theme.
- Voting screens use the new theme.
- Final guess screens use the new theme.
- Results screens use the new theme.
- Statistics and history screens use the new theme.

Functional checks

- Start a complete match.
- Test normal and Imposter role reveals.
- Test Imposter hints.
- Test typed and verbal clue modes.
- Test voting and Skip Vote.
- Test ties.
- Test multiple Imposters.
- Test repeated rounds.
- Test final guessing.
- Test match completion.
- Test history and statistics.
- Refresh or reopen the application and verify saved data.

Technical checks

- No new runtime errors.
- No broken navigation.
- No missing assets.
- No horizontal overflow on mobile.
- No broken buttons.
- No accidental changes to game mechanics.

---

15. FINAL CHANGE CONTROL

Before finishing:

- Review every modified file.
- Confirm that changes are primarily visual.
- Confirm that no gameplay logic was unnecessarily modified.
- Confirm that all existing settings and saved data remain intact.
- Remove unnecessary dependencies or unused assets introduced during development.
- Verify that the design is consistent across all screens.

If a requested visual improvement requires modifying gameplay logic or stored data, stop and explain why before proceeding.

If a screen cannot be safely updated without risking existing functionality, report that screen instead of rewriting its logic.

FINAL EXPECTATION

Transform the existing IMPOSTER game into a polished Premium Editorial experience.

The final visual identity should combine:

- Warm ivory backgrounds.
- Soft cream and beige gradients.
- Subtle paper texture.
- Forest-green elements.
- Electric-lime highlights.
- Elegant typography.
- Refined cards.
- Beautiful buttons.
- Consistent styling across every screen.

The application should feel premium, modern, cohesive and professionally designed.

MOST IMPORTANT: Change the appearance, NOT THE GAME. Preserve 100% of the existing gameplay functionality and behaviour.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
